organism_context: EcoCyc/Escherichia coli-derived reaction entry
rationale: MetaCyc/EcoCyc RXN0-7141 carries only a partial EC (1.17.1.-, CH/CH2 oxidoreductase with NAD+ acceptor) and names no protein, and literature searches found no enzyme interconverting D-ribulose 5-phosphate and 1-deoxy-D-xylulose 5-phosphate. Enzyme identity is genuinely unknown.
direction_note: MetaCyc itself curates this as D-ribulose 5-phosphate + NADH -> 1-deoxy-D-xylulose 5-phosphate + H2O, matching ModelSEED's '<'; the LLM's forward call would require NAD+-dependent hydroxylation of an unactivated methyl group using water, which is not plausible chemistry for this substrate.

enzyme_name: glutathione--homocystine transhydrogenase (EC 1.8.4.1; thiol-disulfide oxidoreductase, glutaredoxin/thioltransferase-type activity)
organism_context: classically described in mammalian liver; the activity is a single GSH-dependent disulfide reduction
rationale: KEGG EC 1.8.4.1 is active and defines exactly this reaction (2 glutathione + homocystine = glutathione disulfide + 2 homocysteine); the catalysing protein is only loosely defined (glutaredoxin/thioltransferase-type thiol-disulfide exchange), but it is a single oxidoreductase activity, so enzyme identity rather than functionality is the weak point.
direction_note: Glutathione disulfide is missing from the ModelSEED equation (status MI:C:-20/H:-26/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2); thiol-disulfide exchange of this kind is freely reversible and its direction is set by the GSH/GSSG and homocysteine/homocystine pools, and MetaCyc also curates it as reversible.

organism_context: Scutellaria baicalensis / S. viscidula flavone-specific plant beta-glucuronidase; oroxylin A 7-O-glucuronide is a secondary substrate
rationale: MetaCyc assigns EC 3.2.1.167 to this reaction and the KEGG EC entry states that oroxylin A 7-O-beta-D-glucuronide is hydrolysed by the same flavone-specific glucuronidase (with lower efficiency than baicalin). A single glycoside hydrolase active site, no second catalytic activity.
direction_note: A glycoside hydrolase only hydrolyses; ModelSEED's '<' would have it condense free D-glucuronate with the aglycone, which glucuronidases do not do physiologically.

organism_context: fungi (Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Candida albicans); the ergosterol biosynthesis II route in which Delta-24(28) reduction precedes Delta-22 desaturation, so ergosta-5,7-dienol is the direct ERG5 substrate
rationale: The ergosta-5,7-dienol -> ergosterol step is the C-22 desaturation run by the cytochrome P450 ERG5/CYP61, a single monooxygenase active site; its NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase partner is a separate polypeptide, so this is not a fused bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: MetaCyc/ModelSEED model the desaturation as an NADP+-dependent dehydrogenation (EC 1.3.1.-) that *produces* NADPH, whereas real ERG5 consumes O2 and NADPH; the dropped O2 is exactly what makes the step irreversible in the biosynthetic (left-to-right) direction.

organism_context: bacteria (E. coli CodA, Zn-dependent) and yeast (S. cerevisiae Fcy1, Fe-dependent); basis of the 5-fluorocytosine/5-fluorouracil prodrug conversion, absent from mammals
rationale: MetaCyc assigns EC 3.5.4.1 and the chemistry is the textbook cytosine deaminase reaction on the 5-fluoro analogue; CodA and Fcy1 are homo-oligomers of one catalytic subunit with a single hydrolytic deamination activity. Called from established knowledge plus the MetaCyc EC.
direction_note: Hydrolytic deamination releasing ammonia is effectively irreversible; ModelSEED's '<' would re-aminate 5-fluorouracil to 5-fluorocytosine, which the enzyme does not do.

enzyme_name: KdgF, unsaturated monouronate ketonization (linearization) enzyme, cupin superfamily
organism_context: pectinolytic and alginolytic bacteria (alginate and pectin utilization loci)
rationale: Hobbs et al. showed KdgF catalyses conversion of pectin- and alginate-derived 4,5-unsaturated monouronates to their linear ketonized forms (here 4-deoxy-L-erythro-5-hexoseulose uronate), a step previously assumed spontaneous; it is a single metal-dependent tautomerization/ring-opening activity.
direction_note: Both the enzymatic and the spontaneous background reaction run from the 4,5-unsaturated uronate to the linear DEH form, i.e. left-to-right as ModelSEED writes it.

organism_context: mammalian noradrenergic/chromaffin secretory vesicles; 4-hydroxyamphetamine is a well-documented alternative substrate giving 4-hydroxynorephedrine
rationale: MetaCyc assigns EC 1.14.17.1 (dopamine beta-monooxygenase) to this beta-hydroxylation of 4-hydroxyamphetamine; DBH is a copper monooxygenase with one catalytic activity. Its paralogue PAM (PHM + PAL) is the bifunctional member of this copper-monooxygenase family - DBH itself is not.
direction_note: The oxidized ascorbate co-product and one ascorbate are missing (status MI:C:-6/H:-6/O:-6), but O2 is on the left-hand side and an O2-consuming copper monooxygenase is irreversible, so the forward sense is secure.

enzyme_name: quinoxaline-2-carboxylic acid (QXC)-activating adenylation enzyme of the echinomycin/triostin A NRPS system (Ecm1-type)
organism_context: Streptomyces spp. producing quinomycin-family bisintercalators (echinomycin, triostin A)
rationale: MetaCyc gives only EC 2.7.7.- for this QXC adenylation step and names no protein; I could not establish whether the activity sits on a free-standing adenylate-forming (ANL-superfamily) protein or on a multidomain NRPS that would also carry a catalytic condensation domain, so mono- vs bifunctional is genuinely unresolved.
direction_note: Adenylation is reversible in isolation (the basis of ATP-PPi exchange assays) but is pulled forward in vivo by PPi hydrolysis and immediate thioesterification, so the forward sense MetaCyc curates is the physiological one.

rationale: MetaCyc RXN-19922 (SAM + glutathione -> S-methylglutathione + S-adenosyl-homocysteine + H+) carries only EC 2.1.1.- and no protein; the obvious candidate, thiopurine methyltransferase, was explicitly shown NOT to S-methylate glutathione, and no alternative catalyst surfaced in the literature.
direction_note: The methyl acceptor product S-methylglutathione is missing from the ModelSEED equation (status MI:C:-11/H:-16/N:-3/O:-6/S:-1); regardless of which protein does it, SAM-to-SAH methyl transfer is effectively irreversible in the left-to-right sense.

enzyme_name: class A non-specific acid phosphatase acting as a pyrophosphate:L-ascorbate 2-phosphotransferase (e.g. Pseudomonas aeruginosa PaAPase)
organism_context: bacterial non-specific acid phosphatases used industrially to make L-ascorbate 2-phosphate from ascorbate plus pyrophosphate
rationale: The only documented enzymes running 'ascorbate phosphorylation' with PPi as donor are bacterial class A non-specific acid phosphatases working in transphosphorylation mode; transfer of the phosphoryl group to water or to ascorbate uses the same single phospho-enzyme active site, so this is one catalytic activity (identity inferred from the chemistry, not from a MetaCyc enzyme assignment).
direction_note: The phosphorylated product (L-ascorbate 2-phosphate) is absent from the ModelSEED equation entirely; the real chemistry consumes PPi (left) and releases Pi (right), i.e. left-to-right.

organism_context: chlorocatechol-degrading proteobacteria running the modified ortho-cleavage pathway (e.g. Pseudomonas chlororaphis RW71, Ralstonia eutropha JMP134)
rationale: MetaCyc assigns EC 5.5.1.- to this cycloisomerization of 2,3,5-trichloro-cis,cis-muconate to its chlorinated dienelactone; chloromuconate cycloisomerases are single-active-site enolase-superfamily enzymes, and the accompanying chloride elimination happens inside the same catalytic cycle rather than as a second activity. Enzyme identity inferred from pathway and EC rather than confirmed for this exact substrate.
direction_note: Degradative flux runs muconate -> lactone; ModelSEED's '<' is the ring-opening sense, which the pathway does not use.

organism_context: plants (flavonol acylglucoside biosynthesis); the closest characterized relative, tea CsHCT, makes the 6''-O-p-coumaroyl isomer of the same glucoside
rationale: MetaCyc names the activity but gives only EC 2.3.1.- and no protein; the chemistry (4-coumaroyl-CoA -> ester + CoA on a flavonol 3-O-glucoside) is diagnostic of a BAHD acyltransferase, a family that is uniformly single-active-site, so 'monofunctional' is inferred from the enzyme class rather than confirmed for a named protein.
direction_note: Acyl-CoA-dependent BAHD transfer is driven by thioester cleavage and is not run backwards from free CoA, so '<' is not a physiological direction.

organism_context: fused as the pentafunctional AROM polypeptide (ARO1) in fungi; a separate monofunctional AroA in bacteria and in plant plastids
rationale: In fungi this reaction is run by one of the five catalytic domains of the single-chain pentafunctional AROM protein (Duncan et al. showed AROM is a mosaic of monofunctional domains); in bacteria and plants the same reaction is run by a monofunctional AroA, so the lineage decides.
direction_note: The product EPSP is missing from the ModelSEED equation (only Pi remains on the right); the enzyme is readily reversible in vitro, but in vivo flux is always PEP + shikimate 3-phosphate -> EPSP + Pi, i.e. left-to-right. Carrying the reaction on a polyfunctional AROM chain does not reverse it.

organism_context: Mycobacterium tuberculosis and other steroid-degrading actinobacteria; last-steroid-ring step of cholesterol catabolism
rationale: Crowe et al. showed IpdAB hydrolyses COCHEA-CoA by a retro-Claisen-like mechanism to the beta-keto-thioester MeDODA-CoA, which is exactly this product; IpdA and IpdB are two separate subunits of one complex sharing a single catalytic base (Glu105 of the alpha subunit), so this is a multi-subunit complex, not a fused bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: Hydrolytic C-C ring cleavage is irreversible and is the catabolic direction; ModelSEED's '<' would re-close the ring with loss of water.

organism_context: mammalian adrenal chromaffin granules and noradrenergic neuron vesicles (catecholamine biosynthesis)
rationale: This is the canonical DBH reaction (dopamine -> noradrenaline), a copper-dependent monooxygenase with one catalytic activity; the tetramer is built from identical subunits, and the bifunctional member of this family is the paralogue PAM (PHM + PAL), not DBH.
direction_note: The oxidized ascorbate co-product and one ascorbate are missing (status MI:C:-6/H:-6/O:-6), but the O2 on the left already makes the hydroxylation irreversible in the left-to-right sense.

organism_context: Viburnum furcatum Blume; glycoside hydrolase family 1
rationale: Ahn et al. characterized furcatin hydrolase as a GH1 disaccharide-specific acuminosidase that releases p-allylphenol (chavicol) together with the intact apiosyl-glucose disaccharide; a single glycosidase active site, confirmed structurally/computationally by Daiyasu et al.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis only; ModelSEED's '<' would have the glycosidase condense free chavicol with free disaccharide, which is not a physiological direction.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana roots (GH1 family, ER-body localized); MetaCyc assigns EC 3.2.1.21
rationale: Ahn et al. identified BGLU21/22/23 as the scopolin-hydrolysing beta-glucosidases of Arabidopsis roots; these are single-active-site GH1 enzymes. PYK10's additional myrosinase-like substrate range is the same beta-glucosidase chemistry applied to a thioglucoside, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Hydrolysis only; '<' would require glucoside synthesis from free D-glucose, which beta-glucosidases do not do in vivo.

enzyme_name: IolD (3D-(3,5/4)-trihydroxycyclohexane-1,2-dione acylhydrolase) acting with IolB (5-deoxy-D-glucuronate isomerase)
organism_context: Bacillus subtilis iolABCDEFGHIJ myo-inositol catabolic operon and bacterial orthologues
rationale: Yoshida et al. showed the hydrolysis of THcHDO by IolD yields 5-deoxy-D-glucuronate, and that a separate enzyme, IolB, then isomerizes it to 2-deoxy-5-keto-D-gluconate; each protein carries one activity, so the hydrolase step itself is monofunctional.
direction_note: MetaCyc R503-RXN collapses the IolD hydrolysis and the IolB isomerization into one entry, so no single enzyme runs it; both constituent steps go in the catabolic (left-to-right) sense, which makes ModelSEED's '<' wrong either way.

enzyme_name: PatF (phyllostine -> neopatulin converting protein of the patulin cluster)
organism_context: Penicillium expansum / Aspergillus clavatus patulin biosynthetic gene cluster
rationale: Targeted knockouts plus substrate feeding in P. expansum assigned the phyllostine (5,6-epoxygentisylquinone) -> neopatulin (isopatulin) conversion to PatF, a single-step cluster protein with no evidence of a second catalytic activity; MetaCyc itself lists no EC for the step.
direction_note: Biosynthetic flux is phyllostine -> neopatulin -> E-ascladiol -> patulin, i.e. left-to-right as ModelSEED writes it.

enzyme_name: unidentified (ring opening of (+)-bisdechlorogeodin to asterric acid)
organism_context: Aspergillus terreus and related fungi, geodin/asterric acid branch of the emodin family of polyketides
rationale: MetaCyc RXN-13554 carries no EC and names no enzyme, and I found no characterized protein for the hydrolytic opening of the bisdechlorogeodin spiro-ring to asterric acid; the step is generally depicted as a facile, possibly non-enzymatic, opening downstream of sulochrin/dihydrogeodin oxidase.
direction_note: Whether enzymatic or spontaneous, the chemistry runs bisdechlorogeodin + H2O -> asterric acid; re-closure of the spiro-lactone with loss of water is not observed in the pathway.

enzyme_name: none identified (the only relevant enzyme, echinocandin B deacylase, catalyses the opposite reaction)
organism_context: Actinoplanes utahensis / Streptomyces echinocandin B deacylase (Ntn-hydrolase) is used to make the echinocandin B nucleus; anidulafungin is then produced by chemical re-acylation of that nucleus
rationale: MetaCyc RXN-16525 is written echinocandin B nucleus -> anidulafungin with no EC and no enzyme - that is the industrial semisynthetic acylation, not an enzymatic step - while the only characterized enzyme in this chemistry, echinocandin B deacylase, runs deacylation in the opposite sense.
direction_note: The entire C24 acyl donor/leaving group is absent from the equation (status MI:C:24/H:21/O:2), and the curated direction is a chemical acylation while the only relevant enzyme runs the reverse, so neither the LLM's nor ModelSEED's call can be supported on enzymology.

enzyme_name: trichothecene acetylesterase (carboxylesterase); TRI8 in Fusarium, intestinal/hepatic carboxylesterases in mammals
organism_context: Fusarium graminearum / F. sporotrichioides trichothecene pathway (TRI8 removes C-3 acetyl in 15-ADON chemotypes and C-15 acetyl in 3-ADON chemotypes); mammalian gut and liver carboxylesterases also deacetylate 15-ADON to DON
rationale: MetaCyc assigns only EC 3.1.1.- to the 15-ADON -> DON deacetylation; the candidate enzymes (Fusarium TRI8, mammalian carboxylesterases) are all single-activity serine hydrolases, but which one runs this exact step is not pinned down.
direction_note: Water and the released acetate are missing from the ModelSEED equation (status MI:C:-2/H:-2/O:-1); ester hydrolysis releasing acetate is irreversible and runs 15-ADON -> DON, i.e. left-to-right.

organism_context: Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 (slr0088) and other cyanobacteria; a CrtI carotene-desaturase-family protein, unrelated in sequence to CrtW-type ketolases
rationale: Fernandez-Gonzalez et al. showed slr0088/CrtO is a beta-carotene ketolase that introduces a single keto group to give echinenone and has no detectable desaturase activity on phytoene, hydroxyneurosporene or zeta-carotene - one catalytic activity on one polypeptide.
direction_note: Carotenoid ketolation is biosynthetic and effectively irreversible; the plastoquinone/water formulation MetaCyc uses is mass- and redox-balanced and consistent with CrtO's CrtI-desaturase-family mechanism (quinone as electron acceptor), so no cofactor is being faked away.

enzyme_name: PhsA (phosphinothricin tripeptide synthetase I, PTTS I), N-acetyldemethylphosphinothricin-activating NRPS module
organism_context: Streptomyces viridochromogenes Tue494 / DSM 40736, bialaphos (phosphinothricin tripeptide) biosynthesis
rationale: Grammel et al. and Schwartz et al. showed PhsA/PTTS I is a 66-76 kDa stand-alone single-module peptide synthetase that activates N-acetyl-demethylphosphinothricin as the adenylate and then the thioester; the adenylation domain carries the only catalytic activity (the carrier/PCP domain is not catalytic), and it is too small to contain a condensation domain.
direction_note: Adenylation is reversible in isolation but is pulled forward by PPi release and thioesterification; ModelSEED's '<' would regenerate ATP from the acyl-adenylate, which is not the physiological sense.

enzyme_name: unidentified (emodin anthrone dimerization to emodin dianthrone)
organism_context: Hypericum perforatum hypericin pathway; the long-proposed catalyst Hyp-1 is a PR-10 ligand-binding protein whose role has been contradicted
rationale: MetaCyc RXN-14896 carries only EC 4.2.1.- and no protein; Hyp-1, the historically proposed 'phenolic oxidative coupling protein', is now regarded as a non-limiting PR-10 protein rather than the dimerizing enzyme, and no replacement catalyst has been identified, so this may well be a spontaneous oxidative phenol coupling.
direction_note: Hypericin biosynthesis runs emodin anthrone -> emodin dianthrone -> protohypericin -> hypericin, so the condensation (left-to-right) direction is the physiological one.
